lesson: Never hold a long option wing without its paired short filling first. D2: BTO XLF260918C00060000 filled @0.15, but the paired STO 59C was rejected (403 'account not eligible for uncovered') — she carried a naked long wing as a 'book'. Rule: in any legged combo, submit the SHORT/income leg first and only submit the long leg after the short confirms; if the short gets rejected (403/422), do NOT fill the remaining leg — abort and enter the position only next session via a mleg-supported combo. Cost: $5 loss plus unwanted delta for a full day.
parting_quote: I buy insurance before I confirm the payout exists — flip that and I'm still employed.

lesson: Cap protective-leg chase at 3 repricings or 8 minutes, whichever first. D2: short 58P filled fat at 0.43, then the long 57P chase went 0.07 (canceled) → 0.12 (canceled) → 0.15 (filled 0.14) — paying 2x plan for the seatbelt sliced the net credit to 0.29 vs the 0.31 market. Rule: enter both legs together; if combo 422s, leg the short first, then place the long ONCE at mid with 3-min TIF; if it can't fill within +$0.03 of fair, close the short immediately flat rather than hold an unpaired short. Also: one full refile max when a combo is rejected — re-quote, don't escalate.
parting_quote: The house beat the quote on one step and robbed me on the other; next time both steps land where I drew them or I sit the dance out.

lesson: Underwrite to the account's rules, not the strategy's math. D2: the QQQ 678P short needed $67,534 cash-secured (6.7x her whole book) and the 744C short was barred as uncovered — both short wings 403'd, leaving two naked longs (668P @1.67, 754C @0.72) that bled $39. Rule: before underwriting any short-premium structure, verify each short wing against the account matrix (cash-secured reserve = strike x 100 for puts; uncovered call eligibility for calls) and required margin under 40% buying-power cap. On a $10K book, QQQ shorts are structurally impossible — cap short-premium underwriting at underlyings where strike*100 <= 60% of allocation.
parting_quote: A plan that only works in a bigger room isn't a plan. It's a costume.

lesson: Stock leg without its call by 10:30 = hedge or exit, never ride unhedged. D2: bought 100 XLF @57.85 at 9:39, then left the 61C STO resting at 0.08 (bid was 0.07) all session — the stock bleed to 57.72 mark became a full −$71 with zero premium banked. Rule: premium order goes in as GTC at mid (0.075), gets ONE repricing to bid+0.01 at 10:30, and if still unfilled by 11:00 either the stock gets hedged down to half size or exited. Being long 100 shares with no credit is not a covered call, it's a long-only bet wearing a covered call's name.
parting_quote: I wanted the position more than I wanted the terms.

lesson: The house trades at the market's spread, never inside it. D2: weekly 59C STO rested at 0.12 with the bid at 0.10 — never crossed; on a 4-day weekly that's 17% of expected premium left on the table for a fill that never comes. Rule: weekly premium orders price at the bid-mid midpoint on entry, one repricing to bid allowed after 15 minutes, then TAKE THE BID. Selling at 0.10 instead of waiting for 0.12 turns −$71 into roughly −$65 and, more importantly, book value = filled premium. A priced edge you never fill is not an edge.
parting_quote: The house takes the market's price — nobody owes me my own.

lesson: Rent clears early or it doesn't exist. D2: 60.5C credit rested 0.14 (a tick over the 0.13 bid) for the whole session — zero income on an unhedged 100-share book that lost $71; the two kept covered-call desks (Roma, Elwood) survived minus $5 precisely because their cash-secured puts filled at 0.36/0.19 immediately. Rule: entry hour is credit hour — premium order placed at market-mid within 60 seconds of the stock fill, single reprice to bid after 15 minutes, take the bid by 10:00. On 15-18 DTE that's ~$11-14 of rent; the difference between a kept book (−$5) and a fired one (−$71) is exactly that fill.
parting_quote: A penny early is the fee. A penny late is a sermon.

lesson: Read the pond before buying it. D2: bought 100 XLP @85.2875 (a good fill, 11c under cap) the same morning the wire printed hawkish rates (Sept hike odds ~56%, 2Y 4.36%) — staples are the most rate-sensitive long you can hold, so the entry was a good fill in a bad pond: −$79, worst on the floor, while sitting completely still. Rule: a macro gate belongs BEFORE sector selection — if the prior session's tape says yields up + hike odds >50%, staples/defensives get halved (50 shares max) or skipped; deploy the freed capital into the sector the rates tape is paying for. The asset was the mistake, not the fill.
parting_quote: There's no bad fill, only bad pond — check which way the water drains before you pick it.
